The Silent Revenue Recovery System, Toronto

You scanned the poster because something in your business slips through the cracks. A call you couldn't pick up. A quote request that sat until the next morning. An invoice that's three weeks late. A happy customer you never asked for a review.

Each of those is money you already earned the chance to collect. This page shows the five automations that catch them. You can build them yourself with the guide below, or I can have them installed for you in your own accounts for a one-time fee, with no monthly retainer.

The five leaks, and what catches each one

1. Missed calls. When you miss a call, the caller gets a text from your business number within seconds: "Sorry we missed you, how can we help?" They can answer by text while you're on the job, before they try the next name on the list.

2. Slow replies to new leads. A form, email or Facebook lead gets a reply within 5 minutes, with your booking link in it. The reply is written by AI from your own words and services, and you see every message it sends.

3. Unpaid invoices. Your invoicing tool sends a polite reminder with a payment link 1 day, 3 days and 7 days after the due date while the invoice stays unpaid, so you stop chasing by phone.

4. Reviews you never asked for. About 2 hours after a job is marked done, every customer gets a thank-you and your Google review link. Every customer gets the same message. Google's rules don't allow businesses to ask only the happy ones, so this asks everyone.

5. Not knowing your numbers. Every Monday at 7:00 AM you get a one-page email: new leads, missed calls caught, invoices paid and outstanding, and new reviews.

The guarantee

If the system doesn't recover at least 50% of your missed leads in your first 30 days, I refund your setup fee and you keep everything built.

Here's how it's counted. A missed lead is a call to your business number that nobody answers, or a message through your connected form. Each number counts once a day, and spam doesn't count. It's recovered when that person replies to the automatic text or email, calls back and gets through, or books, within 48 hours. The count comes from your own call log, text log and lead sheet, and it's in your Monday email every week.

Build it yourself

If you'd rather do it yourself, here's the plan. You'll need an automation tool (Make or Zapier), a texting service (such as Twilio), an AI model for the lead replies, and your own CRM and invoicing tool.

Missed-call text-back. Use a phone number that can send a signal when a call is missed. Set your automation to fire on a missed or no-answer call and send a short text from your business number.

Instant lead reply. Connect your website form, email and Facebook leads to your automation tool. Pass each new lead to an AI prompt that reads the request, sorts it and drafts a short reply with your booking link. Have it send within 5 minutes.

Invoice chasing. Connect your invoicing tool (QuickBooks, Stripe or Square). Schedule reminders at 1, 3 and 7 days past due while the invoice is unpaid, each with a payment link.

Review requests. Trigger on a job marked complete in your CRM or dispatch tool. Wait about 2 hours, then send a thank-you with your Google review link to every customer.

Monday dashboard. Pull your missed-call log, lead count, payments and reviews into one summary, scheduled for Monday at 7:00 AM.

Every text and email carries your business name and a way to opt out. Canada's anti-spam law and US carrier rules both apply to business texting, and the install handles that set-up for you.
